extracted.intended_audience: trademark/classification examiners, IP practitioners, and information specialists who index figurative elements (Vienna Classification users)
extracted.subtask_description: Applying the Vienna Classification (5th Edition) to classify figurative elements (people, animals, plants, landscapes, buildings, foodstuffs, textiles, etc.) appearing in marks or images; use the stated divisions, principal sections and auxiliary sections to select the correct class code(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.3 WOMEN
rubrics_metrics.description: Heads, busts; nuns, nurses; women wearing folk or historical costume; nude women or women wearing underclothes, bathing costume, or other light attire; women wearing a long dress; women engaging in sport, women dancers, drum majorettes; women wearing a kimono, sari, djellaba. Principal sections include many numbered subsections (2.3.1–2.3.25) for variants (city clothes, cooking/housework, agricultural work, sewing/spinning/knitting, office work, other professionals, mounted on animals, allegorical female personages, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary sections (A 2.3.x) cover heads in silhouette, women at their toilet/making up, women in profile/silhouettes, seated/kneeling/lying down, drinking/eating, smoking, stylized women, several women, etc.; includes note that certain specific situations are placed in their appropriate sections; preserves original numbered subsections and auxiliary associations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.5 CHILDREN
rubrics_metrics.description: Heads, busts; boys; girls; children wearing folk/historical/cowboy costume; children in working costume or uniforms; babies; children engaging in sport/playing; children with musical instruments; children with animals; other children (2.5.1–2.5.25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Not including adolescents (they are classified in divisions 2.1, 2.3 or 2.7). Auxiliary sections A 2.5.17–A 2.5.24 cover children seated/kneeling/on all fours, drinking/eating, crying, pairs of children of different sexes, stylized children, several children.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.7 MIXED GROUPS, SCENES
rubrics_metrics.description: Groups composed of men, women and/or children, or any group that gives the impression of a scene; includes heads or busts of man and woman (couple), man and woman in costume, woman(s) and baby(ies), couples, family groups, sporting scenes, groups of workers in fields/forests, indoor scenes, battle scenes, theatre/variety/concert/dancing scenes, travelling shows/fairs/street scenes, groups with vehicles, groups with animals, stylized groups, other groups or scenes (2.7.1–2.7.25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: (a) A group composed solely of men, women or children is placed in the appropriate single-sex division unless it represents a mixed group; (b) any group conveying a scene will be placed in division 2.7. Auxiliary sections (A 2.7.x) include man and woman nude or wearing underclothes (A 2.7.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.9 PARTS OF THE HUMAN BODY, SKELETONS, SKULLS
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearts; eyes (with/without eyebrows/tears); ears; noses; lips/mouths/tongues; teeth/dentures; feet/toes/leg impressions; bodies or dummies without head or feet; skeletons/parts of skeletons/bones; skulls; lungs (respiratory system); hair, locks, wigs, beards, moustaches; hands, cupped hands, fingers, hand imprints, arms, and other parts (2.9.1–2.9.25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Heads are not included here and are instead placed in appropriate sections of divisions 2.1, 2.3, 2.5 or 2.7. Auxiliary sections (A 2.9.15–A 2.9.17) cover open hands, hands joined in handshake, imprints of hands/fingers.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3 ANIMALS (CATEGORY OVERVIEW)
rubrics_metrics.description: General notes and structure for classifying animal depictions: quadrupeds series I–V, quadrumana, parts of bodies/skeletons/skulls of quadrupeds/quadrumana, birds/bats, aquatic animals/scorpions, reptiles/amphibia/snails/seals, insects/spiders/micro-organisms, other animals and groups spanning different divisions (divisions 3.1–3.17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: (a) Heads of quadrupeds/quadrumana placed in appropriate series divisions (3.1–3.5) not in 3.6.25; (b) written/typographical matter representing an animal is classified under 27.3.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.1 QUADRUPEDS (SERIES I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lions; tigers/other large felines; cats/other small felines; dogs/wolves/foxes; bears; pandas; heads of animals of Series I (3.1.1–3.1.16).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary sections include heraldic lions (A 3.1.2) and many A 3.1.x entries covering postures (standing, lying, sitting, rearing, bounding), animals with forepaws resting on objects, animals facing each other, stylized animals, animals in costume, and breed-specific auxiliaries (boxers, poodles, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.2 QUADRUPEDS (SERIES II)
rubrics_metrics.description: Elephants/mammoths; hippopotamus/rhinoceros; giraffes; okapis; camels/dromedaries/llamas; heads of Series II animals (3.2.1–3.2.15).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary sections include elephants facing front, two elephants facing each other (A 3.2.3, A 3.2.4) and stylized/in-costume variants (A 3.2.24, A 3.2.25).

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.3 QUADRUPEDS (SERIES III)
rubrics_metrics.description: Horses, mules; donkeys; zebras; heads of Series III animals (3.3.1–3.3.15).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary sections (A 3.3.17, A 3.3.24, A 3.3.25) cover rearing/bounding postures, stylized animals, and animals in costume.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.4 QUADRUPEDS (SERIES IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bovines (cows, calves, bisons, bulls, other bovines); deer/stags/elk/reindeer/fawns/antelopes; goats/sheep/moufflons/chamois; pigs/boars/warthogs; heads with/without horns and other series IV animals (3.4.1–3.4.20).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary sections specify breed/groupings (cows, bisons), heads of stags (A 3.4.14–A 3.4.16), and postures (lying, bounding, charging), stylized animals, animals in costume (A 3.4.19, A 3.4.22–A 3.4.25).

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.5 QUADRUPEDS (SERIES V), QUADRUMANA
rubrics_metrics.description: Rabbits, hares; squirrels; beavers, marmots, badgers, martens, mink; rats, mice, moles; hedgehogs, porcupines; pangolins, anteaters; kangaroos, koalas; monkeys, apes, orangutans and other quadrumana; other quadrupeds (3.5.1–3.5.20).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary sections include stylized animals and animals in costume (A 3.5.24, A 3.5.25) and heads of Series V (3.5.20).

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.6 PARTS OF THE BODIES, SKELETONS, SKULLS OF QUADRUPEDS OR QUADRUMANA
rubrics_metrics.description: Parts of the bodies, skeletons and skulls of quadrupeds/quadrumana; paws, feet, pawprints, footprints; hides, furs, skins, and other parts (3.6.1–3.6.25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Heads are not included here (they belong to 3.1–3.5). Auxiliary sections include specific items such as hides/furs/skins (A 3.6.11) and other parts (A 3.6.25).

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.7 BIRDS, BATS
rubrics_metrics.description: Eagles, falcons, vultures, condors; cocks/hens/chickens; turkeys/peacocks/hoopoes; owls; ducks/geese/swans; storks/herons/cranes/flamingos or other waders; penguins; albatross/cormorants/gulls/pelicans; swallows; parrots/budgerigars/toucans; birds in flight or with outspread wings; doves/pigeons; ostriches; parrots and other named birds; wings (stylized or not); parts of birds, feathers, footprints, skeletons; nests, bird cages; bats (3.7.1–3.7.23).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: wings constituting symbols/emblems are included; does not include wheels with wings or Mercury's helmet (cross-references given). Auxiliary sections cover heraldic eagles (A 3.7.2), stylized birds, and birds in costume (A 3.7.24–A 3.7.25). Nests with eggs included; eggs alone classified elsewhere (8.7.11).

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.9 AQUATIC ANIMALS, SCORPIONS
rubrics_metrics.description: Fish and fish-like animals; parts of fish/fishbones; sea horses; inkfish/octopuses; crustaceans (crabs, shrimps, crayfish, lobsters), scorpions; starfish; shellfish (oysters, mussels, conches); coral/coral reefs; groups of aquatic animals; aquariums/terrariums/vivariums containing animals of division 3.9; other aquatic animals (3.9.1–3.9.23).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: excludes aquatic animals classified in other divisions (3.7, 3.11, 3.13). Auxiliary sections A 3.9.2–A 3.9.12 list sharks, cetaceans, dolphins, swordfish, ornamental fish, flat fish, eel-like fish, groups of fish, fish in their element, etc. Stylized and in-costume auxiliaries exist (A 3.9.24–A 3.9.25).

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.11 REPTILES, AMPHIBIA, SNAILS, SEALS, SEA LIONS
rubrics_metrics.description: Serpents; snails/slugs; worms; alligators/caymans/crocodiles; chameleons/lizards/salamanders; tortoises; toads/frogs/tadpoles; seals/sea lions; groups and terrariums/vivariums; other animals of division 3.11 (3.11.1–3.11.23).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary sections include serpent-and-cup (medical symbol) and serpent(s) with staff (A 3.11.2–A 3.11.3). Stylized/in-costume auxiliaries available (A 3.11.24–A 3.11.25).

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.13 INSECTS, SPIDERS, MICRO-ORGANISMS
rubrics_metrics.description: Butterflies; other insects and spiders; beehives/cells of honeycombs; micro-organisms; groups of insects/spiders/micro-organisms; specific insect groups (bees/wasps, dragonflies, flies, mosquitoes, beetles, cockroaches, cicadas, ants, lice, caterpillars, cocoons/chrysalises) (3.13.1–3.13.23).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary sections list many insect subgroups (A 3.13.4–A 3.13.23). Stylized insects/spiders and those in costume have auxiliaries (A 3.13.24–A 3.13.25).

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.15 OTHER ANIMALS; LARGE PREHISTORIC ANIMALS
rubrics_metrics.description: Other animals not covered in earlier divisions; large prehistoric animals. Note excludes fabulous animals (4.3, 4.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when an animal does not fit prior animal divisions; cross-reference to fabulous animals exceptions is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.17 GROUPS OF ANIMALS CLASSIFIED IN DIFFERENT DIVISIONS OF CATEGORY 3
rubrics_metrics.description: Groups of animals that fall into different series/divisions within Category 3 and thus require a cross-divisional grouping code (3.17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when group includes animals from distinct divisions; auxiliary sections may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4 SUPERNATURAL, FABULOUS, FANTASTIC OR UNIDENTIFIABLE BEINGS (CATEGORY OVERVIEW)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beings that are supernatural, fabulous, fantastic or unidentifiable; excludes human beings and fantastic animals composed of letters/figures (those are in 27.3). Divisions include winged or horned personages, part-human/part-animal beings, fabulous animals, plants/objects/geometrical figures representing a person or animal (masks/fantastic heads), and groups of figurative elements spanning divisions (4.1–4.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-references and exclusions (e.g., dwarfs, allegorical personages) are specified in notes associated with particular divisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.1 WINGED OR HORNED PERSONAGES
rubrics_metrics.description: Winged human heads; winged children (cherubs, cupids); other winged personages; devils or horned personages with or without wings; heads of devils/horned personages (4.1.1–4.1.25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary sections include groups of winged/horned personages classified across sections (4.1.25).

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.2 BEINGS PARTLY HUMAN AND PARTLY ANIMAL
rubrics_metrics.description: Centaurs; sphinx; tritons; sirens/naiads; other beings partly human and partly animal; groups classified across sections (4.2.1–4.2.25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary section A 4.2.2 covers centaurs with bows/arrows/lances; groups and cross-references are noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.3 FABULOUS ANIMALS
rubrics_metrics.description: Winged lions/griffons; dragons; winged horses (Pegasus); other winged quadrupeds; unicorns; monsters with several heads; heads of fabulous animals; phoenixes and other fabulous animals (4.3.1–4.3.25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes auxiliary entries for heads and groups of fabulous animals across sections (4.3.19–4.3.25).

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.5 PLANTS, OBJECTS OR GEOMETRICAL FIGURES REPRESENTING A PERSONAGE OR AN ANIMAL; MASKS OR FANTASTIC/UNIDENTIFIABLE HEADS
rubrics_metrics.description: Personified plants, combinations of plants representing a personage; personified objects or geometrical figures representing a personage; robots of human appearance; other unidentifiable personifications (4.5.1–4.5.15); plants/objects/geometrical figures representing animals; robots resembling animals; masks and fanciful/unidentifiable heads (4.5.11–4.5.21).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes include examples (snowmen, scarecrows, ghosts) and exclusions (dwarfs, allegorical or mythological personages, winged/horned creatures). Cross-references to fabulous animals (4.3) are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.7 GROUPS OF FIGURATIVE ELEMENTS CLASSIFIED IN DIFFERENT DIVISIONS OF CATEGORY 4
rubrics_metrics.description: Groups composed of figurative elements that belong to different divisions within Category 4, requiring cross-divisional grouping codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when a composition includes multiple types of fantastic or unidentifiable beings spanning divisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5 PLANTS (CATEGORY OVERVIEW)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers plants broadly: trees/bushes; leaves/needles/branches; flowers/blossoms; grain/seeds/fruits; vegetables; other plants; decorations made of plants (5.1–5.13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes emphasize exceptions (e.g., not including surfaces/backgrounds covered with repeated figurative plant elements — category 25 references) and provide auxiliary sections for stylized vs. natural depictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5.1 TREES, BUSHES
rubrics_metrics.description: Trees or bushes of triangular/conical shape (firs, cypresses); oblong trees (poplars); other shapes; trees/bushes without leaves; groups of trees/bushes of different shapes; trunks without branches; large branches (5.1.1–5.1.21).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary sections cover one tree/two trees/three trees/more than three or thickets; stylized trees; conifers; deciduous trees; trees in blossom; palm/banana trees; climbing bushes. Note: when a represented group becomes a forest, it is placed in 6.19.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5.3 LEAVES, NEEDLES, BRANCHES WITH LEAVES OR NEEDLES
rubrics_metrics.description: Tobacco leaves; oak leaves; holly leaves; vine, plane, maple leaves; chestnut leaves; trefoils; ferns/palms/wisteria/ginkgo leaves; vine shoots; olive branches; mistletoe sprigs; needles/branches with needles; grouped leaves (5.3.1–5.3.22).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes stylized leaves and auxiliaries for one leaf, two-to-four leaves, more-than-four leaves/scattered/bunches. Note: not including backgrounds covered with repeated leaf elements (25.7.25). Decorations of vine branches are classified elsewhere (5.13.6 vs 5.3.19).

rubrics_metrics.name: 5.5 FLOWERS, BLOSSOMS
rubrics_metrics.description: Roses, lilies, tulips, magnolias, marguerites/sunflowers/daisies, carnations, pansies, lilac, wisteria, edelweiss, gentians, thistles, poppies, chrysanthemums, orchids, lotus, groups of flowers, bunches/sheaves/baskets, flower beds, scattered flowers (5.5.1–5.5.23).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes heraldic flowers; auxiliaries for stylized flowers, single flower, several flowers (with specified exceptions). Note: excludes surfaces/backgrounds covered with repeated flower elements (25.7.25).

rubrics_metrics.name: 5.7 GRAIN, SEEDS, FRUITS
rubrics_metrics.description: Grain and seeds (including coffee beans); ears of cereals/maize; panicles/sheaves of cereals; shell/husk fruits (almonds, peanuts, cocoa, walnuts); cupulate fruits (sweet chestnuts); berries (strawberries, raspberries, blackberries), grapes, oranges/mandarines/grapefruit, lemons, apples, stone fruits (apricots, peaches, plums, dates, mangos, etc.), pears, cherries, pineapples, bananas, olives, melons/watermelons, other fruits, groups/bowls/baskets/jars of fruits (5.7.1–5.7.26).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes include cotton bolls; auxiliaries cover open fruits/slices, single fruit, groups, bowls/baskets, fruits in jars.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5.9 VEGETABLES
rubrics_metrics.description: Carrots; potatoes/other tubers; onions/bulbs (leeks, garlic); tomatoes; beans/peas/lentils; asparagus; cabbages/lettuce/chicory (note on lettuce prepared for immediate consumption classified elsewhere 8.7.7); gourds; aubergines/cucumbers/gherkin/sweet peppers; other vegetables; groups, baskets, vegetables in jars (5.9.1–5.9.26).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary section A 5.9.23 covers a single vegetable. Distinctions drawn between raw vegetables and prepared/served forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5.11 OTHER PLANTS
rubrics_metrics.description: Algae, seaweeds and other plants; roots/ginsengs; mosses/lichens; mushrooms; potato seedlings; grasses; bamboo/reeds/sugar canes/maize canes/vanilla pods (including bamboo shoots); cotton plants; cones/fir cones/hop cones; agaves/aloes; prickly pears; cactus; plants in pots/ornamental stands/window-boxes/tubs (5.11.1–5.11.23).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliaries list many specific plant types and presentations; use appropriate auxiliary for potted/ornamental presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5.13 DECORATIONS MADE OF PLANTS
rubrics_metrics.description: Crowns of leaves/flowers/fruits; crossed palms; crossed branches; decorations of vine branches; garlands, bands, borders, frames made of plants (leaves, flowers, fruits, other plants); Christmas trees/branches; other plant-made decorations (5.13.1–5.13.25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes specify exclusions (e.g., bunches of leaves 5.3.16, bunches of flowers 5.5.23, bowls/baskets of fruits 5.7.25, repeated plant-element backgrounds 25.7.25). Auxiliaries A 5.13.8–A 5.13.11 subdivide garlands by component (leaves, flowers, fruits, other plants).

rubrics_metrics.name: 6 LANDSCAPES (CATEGORY OVERVIEW)
rubrics_metrics.description: Landscapes include mountains/rocks/grottoes; landscapes with water/river/stream; desert or tropical-type landscapes; urban landscapes or village scenes; other landscapes (6.1–6.19).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes clarify placement (e.g., groups of trees vs forests) and cross-references to other categories when composition elements dominate.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.1 MOUNTAINS, ROCKS, GROTTOES
rubrics_metrics.description: Crags, rocks, walls of rocks (not including reefs); mountains and mountain landscapes; volcanoes; grottoes (6.1.1–6.1.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary section A 6.1.4 covers stylized mountains/volcanoes. Note excludes reefs (6.3.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.3 LANDSCAPES WITH WATER, RIVER OR STREAM
rubrics_metrics.description: Lacustrine or maritime scenes; landscapes with running water (rivers, streams, rapids, torrents) and associated scenes like beaches, coasts, bays, islands, reefs, open sea, lakes/seas with mountains, harbors, springs, waterfalls (6.3.1–6.3.20).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: excludes urban/village landscapes with water (6.7.11). Numerous auxiliaries cover specific water settings (A 6.3.2–A 6.3.14).

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.6 DESERT OR TROPICAL-TYPE LANDSCAPES
rubrics_metrics.description: Desert landscapes or landscapes with very sparse vegetation; oases; other tropical-type landscapes (6.6.1–6.6.25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary A 6.6.3 covers other landscapes with palm trees; stylized/auxiliary sections apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.7 URBAN LANDSCAPES OR VILLAGE SCENES
rubrics_metrics.description: Streets; squares; built-up areas; urban or village scenes with water/river/stream; other urban or village scenes (6.7.1–6.7.25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary sections A 6.7.5–A 6.7.8 subdivide built-up areas into skyscrapers, flat-roofed houses, huts, rural constructions. Note: built-up areas composed of skyscrapers etc. have separate auxiliaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.19 OTHER LANDSCAPES
rubrics_metrics.description: Other landscapes not previously classified, including forests/undergrowth, vineyards, other cultivated areas, grasslands/pastures, pasturelands with mountains, landscapes with windmills, houses, factories/industrial constructions, polar landscapes (6.19.1–6.19.19).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: a group of three or more trees that does not represent a forest is placed in 5.1.1–5.1.4 instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7 CONSTRUCTIONS, STRUCTURES, BUILDING MATERIALS (CATEGORY OVERVIEW)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers dwellings/buildings/advertisement hoardings/pillars/cages; parts of dwellings/buildings/interiors; monuments/stadiums/fountains; structural works (bridges, tunnels, roads); building materials, walls, gates, scaffolding (7.1–7.15).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides principal sections and many auxiliary sections for subtypes, stylized variants, ruins, postures and specific structural elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7.1 DWELLINGS, BUILDINGS, ADVERTISEMENT HOARDINGS, CAGES OR KENNELS FOR ANIMALS
rubrics_metrics.description: Castles/fortresses/palaces; churches/cathedrals/abbeys/monasteries; mosques/minarets; pagodas; towers or masts/derricks; houses/skyscrapers; industrial establishments/factory chimneys; filling stations; lighthouses; windmills/water mills; kiosks/shelters/fair booths/market stalls; advertisement hoardings/pillars; huts/cabins; tents/igloos; animals’ cages/kennels; stylized buildings and other dwellings or buildings (7.1.1–7.1.25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: includes transmitting masts; excludes Eiffel Tower (7.5.2) in one example. Auxiliary sections subdivide urban/rural houses, flat-roofed houses, chalets, and dwellings in ruins.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7.3 PARTS OF DWELLINGS OR OF BUILDINGS, INTERIORS
rubrics_metrics.description: Doors/entrances; windows/stained-glass windows; bays/balconies/balustrades/moucharabies; interiors; roofs; chimneys/chimney pots; shop window displays; staircases; blinds/shutters/awnings; kitchens; bathrooms/saunas; bedrooms; cellars; other parts (7.3.1–7.3.25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: excludes factory chimneys (7.1.14) and hearths (13.3.1). Auxiliary sections specify interior types associated with principal sections (A 7.3.5–A 7.3.9).

rubrics_metrics.name: 7.5 MONUMENTS, STADIUMS, FOUNTAINS
rubrics_metrics.description: Pyramids; constructions recognized as monuments (Great Wall of China, Eiffel Tower, Statue of Liberty, etc.); other ancient monuments; stadiums/amphitheaters/playgrounds/playing fields; triumphal arches/porticos/town gates; labyrinths; fountains/basins/swimming pools/sprays/wells; columns/obelisks; ancient temples or parts thereof (7.5.1–7.5.25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary sections include ancient temples/parts and columns/obelisks (A 7.5.6, A 7.5.8); the Eiffel Tower is given as an example placement in monuments.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7.11 STRUCTURAL WORKS
rubrics_metrics.description: Bridges; tunnels; roads/intersections/road forks; railway lines; mooring posts/bollards; dams; other structural works (7.11.1–7.11.25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for public works and infrastructural constructions; auxiliary sections address specific work types.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7.15 BUILDING MATERIALS, WALLS, GATES OR BARRIERS, SCAFFOLDING
rubrics_metrics.description: Stones for building/bricks; planks/plates/panels/flagstones; corrugated iron/other corrugated materials; representations of wood (natural wood surfaces/bark or wood cut with/against grain; ornamental wood backgrounds might be categorized in category 25); tiles; other building materials; walls/gates/barriers; scaffolding (7.15.1–7.15.25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note clarifies representation of wood and cross-references ornamental wood backgrounds to category 25.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8 FOODSTUFFS (CATEGORY OVERVIEW)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers bakers' products/pastry/confectionery/chocolate; milk/dairy/cheeses; butchers’ meat/pork/fishmongers' products; other foodstuffs (8.1–8.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes principal sections for prepared and unprepared food items with auxiliaries for shapes, presentations and specific preparations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.1 BAKERS' PRODUCTS, PASTRY, CONFECTIONERY, CHOCOLATE
rubrics_metrics.description: Bread; rusks/slices/sandwiches; bread rolls/brioches; croissants; small biscuits; pastries; ices; chocolate/confectionery; chewing gum; wafers/ice cream cones; lollipops, pralines, slabs/sticks/squares of chocolate; tarts/flans/pies; cakes; other bakers' products (8.1.1–8.1.25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary sections provide shape/presentation distinctions (pan loaves, long loaves, round loaves), biscuit forms, chocolate forms (slabs, sticks, pralines), and classification of mixtures of small biscuits.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.3 MILK, DAIRY PRODUCTS, CHEESES
rubrics_metrics.description: Milk/cream/whipped cream; butter/margarine (in pats/slabs/shell shapes/other shapes); cheeses (round/square/uncut/cut up); other dairy products (8.3.1–8.3.25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary sections subdivide forms/presentations of butter/margarine and cheese shapes; cross-references exclude certain dairy products classified elsewhere (8.7.15).

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.5 BUTCHERS' MEAT, PORK PRODUCTS, FISHMONGERS' PRODUCTS
rubrics_metrics.description: Butchers' meat, pork products, fishmongers' products including ham/legs/joints of meat; sausages ('fresh', 'dry', salami); meat/pork products in slices; poultry/game prepared for cooking; fish/fish fillets prepared/cooked (8.5.1–8.5.25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary sections list specific product types and other butchers' products (A 8.5.2–A 8.5.25).

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.7 OTHER FOODSTUFFS
rubrics_metrics.description: Soups/beverages; macaroni/pasta; pizzas; dishes or plates filled; dishes of vegetables/vegetable salads; crisps/potato products; eggs; fruit salads/compotes; baked custard/puddings/omelettes; mixtures of foodstuffs classified in different divisions; sugar; pet food (8.7.1–8.7.25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes prepared/served food items and cross-references mixtures and prepared lettuce (noted elsewhere).

rubrics_metrics.name: 9 TEXTILES, CLOTHING, SEWING ACCESSORIES, HEADWEAR, FOOTWEAR (CATEGORY OVERVIEW)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers textiles and clothing items, sewing accessories/patterns, headwear, footwear, and related textile articles (9.1–9.9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principal sections distinguish textiles other than clothing, clothing items, sewing accessories, and auxiliaries detail presentations, edging, stitches, and related textile conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 9.1 TEXTILES OTHER THAN CLOTHING, SHUTTLES
rubrics_metrics.description: Thread; laces/braids/tapes/cords/ropes; stitches/embroidery/trimmings; ribbons/bows; cloth/network/flat linen/curtains/carpets; bed coverings/cushions/eiderdowns; cloth labels; other textile articles (9.1.1–9.1.25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary sections cover thread presentations (skein/bobbin/shuttle/ball), cloth edges, network/loose weaving, cloth in pieces/rolls/piles, draped cloth/curtains, carpets, samples and other textile presentations (A 9.1.2–A 9.1.22).

rubrics_metrics.name: 9.3 CLOTHING
rubrics_metrics.description: General clothing items (jackets/waistcoats/coats, trousers, suits/costumes, dresses/aprons/ladies’ suits, ponchos, pullovers/sweaters, shirts/T-shirts, collars, ties/bow ties/silk scarves, underwear/bathing costumes, gloves, stockings/socks/bootees, belts, bibs, clothing pockets, diving suits, and other clothing) (9.3.1–9.3.26).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary sections subdivide clothing types and specify which items are placed in clothing vs other divisions (e.g., headwear/footwear in their own divisions). Underwear and bathing costumes have specific auxiliaries (A 9.3.14).

rubrics_metrics.name: 9.5 SEWING ACCESSORIES, PATTERNS FOR DRESSMAKING
rubrics_metrics.description: Needles, thimbles, hooks, pins; knitting needles; thimbles; crochet hooks; fastening hooks; safety pins; buttons; press studs; slide fasteners; patterns for clothing; other sewing accessories (9.5.1–9.5.10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes exclude scissors (14.7.18) and tape measures (17.5.1) from this division; auxiliary sections enumerate specific needle types, pins, buttons, press studs, slide fasteners and patterns (A 9.5.2–A 9.5.16). Patterns resembling clothing are placed in 9.3.
